design.claims: Fixed15previouslyknown regression targets; exact same logicalcatalogues/fourlemmabank; normalform changesproofset with statedclosed/global/rooted boundedexistence theorem. Scan/index same markedinventory. No learnedfailuremarks,RL,noveltheorem,fullPA/Hilbert/universalWang claim. Workunitsproxy; singlefixedorder timing; all60positions retained.
design.history: New distinct persistent reproduction after original20261029 rawQfiles becameunavailable; original aggregate receipt is historical only and unadmitted. Current runtime bytehash differs. No old grant/output directory reused.
design.recovery_note: A prior20261029 qualification has a recovered original observer receipt but missing native case/proof files; it is historical receipt-only and unadmitted. This is a distinct persistent reproduction using a changed Python runtime hash, new independent reference and fresh run identities. No old authority is reused.

assessment: This tests explicit normal-form markings. They remove some valid proofs while preserving bounded proof existence under fixed closed context-independent producers. They are not learned failure markings.
The direct and indexed history methods share one marked inventory. Their comparison tests enumeration cost; comparison with unmarked GCTS tests a changed proof set with an existence argument.

The current finite producer catalogue also admits conventional memoized proof search. A geometric encoding alone establishes no complexity advantage. These known regression assertions and one timing observation cannot establish broad superiority over automated theorem provers.

A lower aggregate search time can result from earlier resource refusals and fewer verified proofs. It is not a speedup unless comparable verified outcomes are reached. Positive proof coverage and finite negative closure are reported separately.
No RL policy is trained or used. Learned failure markings, variable connected cluster proposals, one fixed universal proof palette, and substantial arithmetic and Hilbert geometry remain open.
